sn35.101:1.1: “Bhikkhus, whatever is not yours, abandon it.
sn35.101:1.2: When you have abandoned it, that will lead to your welfare and happiness.
sn35.101:1.3: And what is it, bhikkhus, that is not yours?
sn35.101:1.4: The eye is not yours: abandon it.
sn35.101:1.6: When you have abandoned it, that will lead to your welfare and happiness.
sn35.101:1.16: Whatever feeling arises with eye-contact as condition—whether pleasant or painful or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—that too is not yours: abandon it.
sn35.101:1.18: When you have abandoned it, that will lead to your welfare and happiness.
sn35.101:3.13: Whatever feeling arises with mind-contact as condition … that too is not yours: abandon it.
sn35.101:3.15: When you have abandoned it, that will lead to your welfare and happiness.
sn35.101:4.1: “Suppose, bhikkhus, people were to carry off the grass, sticks, branches, and foliage in this Jeta’s Grove, or to burn them, or to do with them as they wish.
sn35.101:4.3: ‘People are carrying us off, or burning us, or doing with us as they wish’?”
sn35.101:7.1: Because, venerable sir, that is neither our self nor what belongs to our self.”
sn35.101:8.1: “So too, bhikkhus, the eye is not yours …
sn35.101:8.7: Whatever feeling arises with mind-contact as condition … that too is not yours: abandon it.
sn35.101:8.9: When you have abandoned it, that will lead to your welfare and happiness.”
